perf-ci: nightly-perf job finished — detected 12% p99 latency regression for model=bert-serve on pool=rtx-dedicated (compare: baseline 88ms -> current 98.6ms). dashboard: https://perf.redwood/example/compare/17478 :eyes:

andrew: ack. grabbing the perf diff and traces now. tagging @zane in case this matches the batching patch from last deploy.

maya: is this from nightly-e2e or the microbench? the artifact shows per-token cost jump around token 512.

zane: microbench. I saw a tail spike yesterday in local runs after the continuous-batching tweak — might be KV cache invalidation boundary. will try to repro.

kira: can someone upload the raw profiling trace? nvprof/nsight would help — or a `torch.profiler` run. also curious whether this is only on RTX nodes or on CPU path too.

andrew: posted logs and perf-snapshots to the CI artifact bundle: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/1747890123/ (big file). small excerpt below:
```
[2025-05-03T03:12:11Z] step=decode seq=1024 batch=1 p99=98.6ms p50=22.4ms
[2025-05-03T03:12:11Z] trace=rtx-3 gpu=0 kernel=attention_sparse time=45.2ms
```

zane: repro command I'm running: `./bin/run_microbench --model bert-serve --seq 1024 --batch 1 --seed 42 --profile nsight`

dylan: @oncall-sre can we spin an rtx-dedicated repro instance on the nightly VLAN so profiling doesn't hit prod GPUs? need 2 hours.

oncall-sre: granted. adding label infra/rtx-nightly. instance id i-rtx-nightly-47. will forward SSH once ready (ETA ~15m).

maya: quick hypothesis — last week's kernel change swapped a matmul kernel that regresses small-batch tail. @zane can you bisect between commits `ef4a9..b7c2d`? if we get a commit we can hotfix revert on dedicated pool.

zane: starting bisection now. will post a short status update in ~30m. if repro, I'll capture nvtx ranges and upload flamegraph.

andrew: if bisection hits the kernel, can we try a quantized fallback path (low-risk) as a temporary mitigation? RedwoodOptimize has a recommended profile for bert-serve: `opt_profile: bert-rtx-low-batch` — worth trying.

kira: agree. also run `export RW_DISABLE_CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=1` as a quick toggle to test whether batching logic causes the spike.

perf-ci: automated note — created perf-issue #PERF-4987 and linked CI artifacts. tagging owners: @eng-runtime.

zane: update: reproduced locally on HEAD, p99 increases ~11% when continuous-batching is enabled. capturing nsight trace now.

andrew: thanks. next steps: (1) nvprof/nsight trace analysis (zane) (2) try disable batching on canary nodes (kira/infra) (3) tentative rollback plan if kernel confirmed (maya) — let's sync in this thread.

dylan: I'll schedule a short async review & decision at 10:00 PT if we don't have a fix by then.

maya: got nvprof output. attaching small flame excerpt -> looks like attention kernel time shifted. will upload full flame in the issue. :mag:

zane: uploaded nsight capture: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/1747890123/nsight.capt. starting flamegraph parse.

andrew: marking this thread in triage as "in-progress", assigning to zane. ping me if you need extra GPU time. :thumbsup:

perf-ci: closing CI alert (auto) — followups tracked in #PERF-4987.

andrew: leaving final note — temporary mitigation plan: disable continuous-batching on dedicated rtx pool for nightly runs until patch. will open a PR for toggling at runtime.

zane: on it, will send PR and link here.

kira: thanks everyone — great async triage. :rocket:
